568:
No building permit, rezoning request or subdivision plan will be approved by the permitting officer unless the permit, request and/or plan is in compliance with the groundwater protection standards listed herein.
(1) Enforcement. The permitting officer, his agent, officers and employees shall have authority to enter upon privately owned land for the purpose of performing their assigned duties and responsibilities under this article, and may take or cause to be made such examinations, surveys or sampling as the permitting officer deems necessary.
a. The permitting officer may require a bond with surety and conditions sufficient to secure compliance with the conditions set forth in the permit. The particular amount and conditions of the bond shall be consistent with the purposes of this article. In the event of a breach of any condition of any such bond, the permitting officer may institute an action in a court of competent jurisdiction upon such bond and prosecute the same to judgment and execution.
b. The permitting officer shall have authority to enforce this article; issue permits hereunder; and address violations or threatened violations hereof by issuance of violation notices, administrative orders and civil and criminal actions. All costs, fees and expenses in connection with such actions may be recovered as damages against the violator.
c. Law enforcement officials or other officials having police powers in the jurisdiction shall have authority to assist the permitting officer in enforcement.
d. The permitting officer shall have the authority to issue cease and desist orders in the event of any violation of this article. Cease and desist orders may be appealed to a court of competent jurisdiction, as identified herein.
e. When the permitting officer determines that a building or other structure has been constructed in violation of this article, the violator may, at the discretion of the permitting officer, be required to remove the structure.
f. When removal of vegetative cover, excavation, or fill has taken place in violation of this article, the violator may be required to restore the affected land to its original contours and to restore vegetation, as far as practicable.
(2) Development permit review and site plan requirement. With the exception of certain exempted activities identified in subsection (4) of this section, applications for a development permit within the groundwater recharge area district shall include a site plan providing the following information:
a. A map drawn to a scale of not less than one inch equals 100 feet showing all planned improvements including the width, depth and length of all existing and proposed structures, roads, watercourses and drainageways, water lines, wastewater and stormwater facilities, and utility installations.
b. Location, dimensions and area of all impervious surfaces, both existing and proposed, on the site.
c. The orientation and distance from the boundaries of the proposed site to the nearest bank of an affected perennial stream or water body.
d. Elevations of the site and adjacent lands within 200 feet of the site at contour intervals of no greater than five feet.
e. Location and detailed design of any spill and leak collection systems designed for the purpose of containing hazardous or toxic materials which may be released accidentally.
f. Calculations of the amount of cut and fill proposed and cross sectional drawings showing existing and proposed grades in areas of fill or excavation. Elevations, horizontal scale and vertical scale must be shown on cross sectional drawings.
(3) Activities to comply with site plan. All development activities or site work conducted after approval of the site plan shall conform with the specifications of said site plan. Significant changes to the site plan that would alter the amount and velocity of stormwater runoff from the site, increase the amount of impervious surface within the development, alter the overall density of development, result in a considerable increase in the amount of excavation, fill or removal of vegetation during construction or otherwise result in an alteration of the overall appearance of the development as proposed, can be amended only with the approval of the permitting officer. Minor changes, such as the realignment of streets or minor alterations to drainage structures and other infrastructure to meet unexpected conditions are exempted from this requirement.
(4) Exemptions to site plan requirements. The following activities and developments are exempt from the requirement for detailed site plans:
a. Any subdivision, multifamily, or group housing development where less than ten dwelling units are proposed.
b. Repair to a facility that is part of a previously approved and permitted development.
c. Construction of minor structures, such as sheds or additions to single-family residences.
(5) Review procedures. The application shall be made to the permitting officer and shall be reviewed within seven days. The review period shall begin with the permitting officer's determination that the application is complete. The review period shall include the preparation of findings; approval, conditional approval or disapproval, by the permitting officer. The applicant will receive written notification of the findings of the permitting officer.
(6) Permit expiration.
a. If construction described in the development permit has not commenced within six months from the date of permit issuance, the permit shall expire.
b. If construction described in the development permit is suspended or abandoned after work has commenced, the permit shall expire six months after the date work ceased.
(Code 1986, § 5-334; Ord. No. O-00-01-02, § 4, 1-20-2000; Ord. No. O-00-06-24, § 4, 6-22-2000)
569:
(a) For all pollution susceptibility areas, new waste disposal facilities must have synthetic liners and leachate collection systems.
(b) New agricultural waste impoundment sites shall be lined if they are within:
(1) A high pollution susceptibility area;
(2) A medium pollution susceptibility area and exceed 15 acre-feet; or
(3) A low pollution susceptibility area and exceed 50 acre-feet.
(c) At a minimum, the liner shall be constructed of compacted clay having a thickness of one foot, and a vertical hydraulic conductivity of less than 5 × 10 -7 cm/sec or other criteria established by the U. S. Department of Agriculture Natural Resources Conservation Service.
(d) No land disposal of hazardous waste shall be permitted within any significant groundwater recharge area.
(e) For all significant groundwater recharge areas the handling, storage and disposal of hazardous materials, as identified in section 312 of the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act of 1976, as amended, excluding underground storage tanks, and in amounts of 10,000 pounds or more on any one day, shall take place on an impermeable surface having spill and leak protection approved by the state department of natural resources, environmental protection division (EPD), and in conformance with local fire prevention code requirements.
(f) For all significant groundwater recharge areas new, above ground chemical or petroleum storage tanks larger than 650 gallons must have secondary containment for 110 percent of tank volume, or 110 percent of the largest tank in a cluster of tanks. Such tanks used for agricultural purposes are exempt from this requirement, provided they comply with applicable federal regulations.
(g) For high pollution susceptibility areas, new wastewater treatment basins shall have an impermeable liner approved by EPD.
(h) For high pollution susceptibility areas no new stormwater infiltration basins may be constructed.
(i) For high pollution susceptibility areas the use of wastewater spray irrigation systems and the land application of wastewater sludge shall be practiced in accordance with department of natural resources criteria for slow rate land treatment. An application for a development permit for activities involving wastewater spray irrigation or land application of wastewater sludge must be accompanied by proof that the applicant has received a land application system permit from EPD.
(j) Minimum lot sizes and septic systems. Construction shall not proceed on any building or structure to be served by an on-site sewage management system until the county health department approves the proposed sewage management system as meeting requirements outlined in section M of the department of human resources (DHR) manual for on-site sewage management systems, incorporated herein by reference, and the required building permits have been issued. (See appendix to Ordinance No. O-00-06-24 for section M requirements.)
(Code 1986, § 5-336; Ord. No. O-00-01-02, § 6, 1-20-2000; Ord. No. O-00-06-24, § 6, 6-22-2000)

(a) The commission shall be comprised of 15 members to be appointed by the governing body of the city. (b) Eight members of the board initially appointed by the governing body shall be appointed for a term of one year. The remaining seven members of the board of the commission shall be initially appointed for terms of two years. The governing body of the city shall determine at the time of appointment which appointed members shall serve initial one year terms and which appointed members shall serve initial two-year terms. Upon the expiration of the terms of the members of the board initially appointed by the governing body, the term of each commission member shall thereafter be two years. No commission member shall serve more than two consecutive terms; provided, however, that a commission member appointed to complete the unexpired term of another commission member shall, at the completion of the unexpired term being served, be eligible for appointment for two full consecutive terms thereafter.
(c) Notwithstanding the foregoing provisions of subparagraph (a) and subparagraph (b) of this section, the board members of the commission as of the effective date of this article shall consist of the board members of the City of Americus Main Street program. Such board members shall serve as the board of the commission until July 1, 2020, or until the governing body appoints members of the board of the commission under subparagraph (b) of this section, whichever shall first occur. While the board of the Main Street Program is serving as the board of the commission, such board shall follow the rules of procedure as established by this article and shall carry out the mission of the commission to the same extent and utilizing the same procedures that are required of the board as provided by this article.

582:

(a) "Consumer fireworks" means small firework devices as more particularly defined in O.C.G.A. § 25-10-1(a)(1). The term "consumer fireworks" shall not include the following:
(1) Model rockets and model rocket engines designed, sold, and used for the purpose of preparing recoverable aero models; toy pistol paper caps in which the explosive contents average 0.25 grains or less of explosive mixture per paper cap or toy pistols; toy canons, toy canes, toy guns, or other devices using such paper caps; nor shall the term "consumer fireworks" include ammunition consumed by weapons used for sporting and hunting purposes; and
(2) Wire or wood sparklers of 100 grams or less mixture per item; other sparkling items which are nonexplosive and nonaerial and contains 75 grams or less of chemical components per tube for a total of 500 grams or less for multiple tubes; snake and glow worms; smoke devices; or trick noise makers which include paper streamers, party poppers, string poppers, snappers, and drop pops each consisting of 0.25 grains or less of explosive mixtures.
(b) Any person, firm, corporation, association, or partnership which desires to undertake the use or ignition of consumer fireworks within the corporate limits of the city shall be required to obtain a special use permit to do so from the city council. The cost of such permit shall be established by the city council, but such cost shall not exceed $100.00 per day for each such permit. No such permit shall be required for use or ignition of consumer fireworks on January 1, the last Saturday and Sunday in May, July 3, July 4, the first Monday in September, and December 31 of each year after the time of 10:00 a.m. and up to and including the time of 11:59 p.m., and on January 1 of each year beginning at the time of 12:00 midnight and up to and including the ending time of 1:00 a.m. The use of consumer fireworks shall be subject to the noise provisions of chapter 62, section 62-110, provided however that the decibel measurement limitations shall not be applicable to consumer fireworks used or ignited during the dates and times specified in subparagraph (b) of this section.
(c) Such special use permits shall designate the time or times and location that such person, firm, corporation, association, or partnership may use or ignite or cause to be ignited such consumer fireworks. Each person, firm, corporation, association, or partnership and each location shall require a separate special use permit.
(d) No such special use permit shall be issued for the use or ignition of consumer fireworks at any location where such consumer fireworks are prohibited as established by O.C.G.A. § 25-10-2(b)(3)(C) or by any other federal or state law or regulation.
(e) No person younger than 18 years shall be authorized to use or ignite or cause to be ignited or possess, manufacture, transport, or store consumer fireworks.
(f) Any person, firm, corporation, association, or partnership which uses, ignites, or causes to be ignited consumer fireworks at a time during which a special permit to do so is required for the location where such fireworks are used or ignited, shall be deemed to be guilty of a misdemeanor in violation of this division and, upon conviction therefor, shall be subject to punishment in accord with the provisions of chapter 1, section 1-8 of this Code.
(Ord. No. 2021-15, 9-23-2021)

(a) Insurers' license fees. There is hereby levied for the year 1995 and for each year thereafter an annual license fee upon each insurer doing business within the city in the amount as established by ordinance. For each separate business location in excess of one, not covered by subsection (b) of this section, which is operating on behalf of such insurers within the city, there is hereby levied a license fee in the amount as established by ordinance. There is hereby levied for the year 1995 and for each year thereafter an annual tax based solely upon gross direct premiums upon each insurer writing life, accident and sickness insurance within the state in an amount equal to one percent of the gross direct premiums received during the preceding calendar year in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 33-8-8.1. Gross direct premiums as used in this section shall mean gross direct premiums as used in O.C.G.A. § 33-8-4. The premium tax levied by this section is in addition to the license fees imposed by subsection (a) of this section.
(e) Same—All other insurers. There is hereby levied for the year 1995 and for each year thereafter an annual tax based solely upon gross direct premiums upon each insurer, other than an insurer transacting business in the class of insurance designated in O.C.G.A. § 33-3-5(2), doing business within the state in an amount equal to 2.5 percent of the gross direct premiums received during the preceding calendar year in accordance with O.C.G.A. § 33-8-8.2. Gross direct premiums as used in this section shall mean gross direct premiums as used in O.C.G.A. § 33-8-4. Such report shall be made over affidavit of an officer of such company. It is hereby declared to be a violation of this section for any person, or the agent of any person to knowingly give false or incomplete information on any such report. Said report shall be filed at the time of paying the license fee and premium tax.
(h) Confidentiality of information. All reports required to be filed under this section shall be confidential and the information contained therein shall be solely for the use of the officers of the city responsible for administering this section.
(i) Penalties. The fees and taxes levied by this section may be enforced by execution in the same manner as other taxes of the city. A violation of this section shall be grounds for refusing or revoking a license, and the person responsible may be punished as for violations of other city ordinances.

The following words, terms and phrases shall, for the purposes of this article and except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning, be defined as follows:
City. The City of Americus and, variously, the incorporated territory of Americus, wherein the city government is empowered to impose this tax by O.C.G.A. § 48-13-50 et seq.
City finance director. The duly appointed city finance director of the city or his designee.
Due date. The 20th day after the close of the monthly period for which the tax is to be computed.
Estimated tax liability. The lodging provider's prospective tax liability based upon the average monthly tax remittance in the prior fiscal year, as adjusted for change in tax rate or substantial change in circumstances due to damage to the hotel.
Folio. Primary documentation produced by a hotel that demonstrates interaction between the lodging provider and the occupant, and which, at a minimum, reflects the name and address given by the occupant, the date(s) of occupancy, the amount of rent charged for each date together with the amounts of applicable excise tax, and the method(s) of payment.
Guest room. Accommodations occupied, or intended, arranged, or designed for transient occupancy, by one or more occupants for the purpose of living quarters or residential use.
Hotel. Any facility or any portion of a facility, including any lodging house, rooming house, dormitory, Turkish bath, bachelor hotel, studio hotel, motel, motor hotel, auto or trailer court, truckstop, tourist cabin, campground, lodge, inn, time-share or other condominium, apartment community, public club, or private club, containing guest rooms and which is occupied, or is intended or designed for occupancy, by paying guests, whether rent is paid in money, goods, labor, or otherwise. It does not include any hospital, asylum, sanitarium, orphanage, jail, prison, or other facility in which human beings are housed and detained under legal restraint.
Lodging provider. Any person operating a hotel in the city including, but not limited to, the owner or proprietor of such premises, lessee, sub-lessee, lender in possession, licensee or any other person operating such hotel; and who is subject to the taxation imposed for furnishing for value to the public any rooms, lodgings, or accommodations.
Monthly period. The calendar months of any year.
Occupancy. The use or possession, or the right to the use or possession of any guest room in a hotel or the right to the use or possession of the furnishings or to the services and accommodations accompanying the use and possession of the guest room.
Occupant. Any person who, for a consideration, uses, possesses, or has the right to use or possess any guest room in a hotel under any lease, concession, permit, right of access, license to use or other agreement, or otherwise.
Permanent resident. Any occupant who, as of a given date, has or shall have occupied or has or shall have the right of occupancy of any guest room in a hotel for not less than 30 continuous days next preceding such date.
Person. Rent. The consideration received for occupancy valued in money, whether received in money or otherwise, including all receipts, cash, credits, and property or services of any kind or nature, and also the amount for which credit is allowed by the lodging provider to the occupant, without any deduction therefrom whatsoever.
Tax. The tax on occupants imposed by this article, as provided for by O.C.G.A. § 48-13-50 et seq., specifically O.C.G.A. § 48-13-51(a).

(a) Due date of taxes. All amounts of such tax shall be due and payable to the City of Americus monthly on or before the 20th day of the month next succeeding the respective monthly period. The tax shall become delinquent for any monthly period after the 20th day of each succeeding month during which it remains unpaid.
(b) Penalty and interest for failure to pay tax by due date. A lodging provider who fails to make any return or to pay the amount of tax as prescribed, shall be assessed a specific penalty to be added to the tax in the amount of five percent or $5.00, whichever is greater, if the failure is for one month or less; and an additional five percent or $5.00, whichever is greater, for each additional month or fraction thereof in which such failure shall continue; provided, however, that the aggregate penalty for any single violation shall not exceed 25 percent or $25.00, whichever is greater. Delinquent amounts shall bear interest at the rate of one percent per month, or fraction thereof, until paid.
(c) Acceptance of delinquent return and remittance without imposing penalty and interest; authority; requirements. If the failure to make any return or to pay the amount of tax by the due date results from providential cause shown to the satisfaction of the governing authority of the city by affidavit attached to the return, and remittance is made within ten days of the due date, such return may be accepted exclusive of penalty and interest.
(d) Waiving of penalty and interest; authority. O.C.G.A. § 48-2-41, relating to the authority to waive interest, and O.C.G.A. § 48-2-43, relating to the authority to waive penalty, shall apply; provided, however, that the governing authority shall stand in lieu of the Georgia Commissioner of Revenue, and the city shall stand in lieu of the state.
(e) Penalty for fraud. In the case of a false or fraudulent return, or of failure to file a return where willful intent exists to defraud the city of any tax due, a penalty of 50 percent of any tax due and unpaid tax shall be assessed.
(f) Return; remittance; time of filing; lodging providers required to file; contents. On or before the 20th day of the month succeeding each monthly period, a return for the preceding monthly period together with appropriate remittance shall be filed with the city finance director. The return shall report the gross rent, taxable rent, exempt rent, amount of tax collected or otherwise due for the period, and such other information as may be required by the city finance director. However, if the estimated tax liability for any monthly period shall exceed $2,500.00 for a lodging provider who, in the prior fiscal year remitted tax greater than $2,500.00 in any three consecutive months, such lodging provider shall file an estimated return and remit not less than 50 percent of the estimated tax liability for the monthly period by the 20th day of that same monthly period. The amount of tax so remitted shall be credited against the amount to be due with the regular return for the monthly period to be filed on the 20th day of the succeeding month.
(g) Extension of time of filing; authority; requirements; remittance; penalty and interest. The governing authority of the city may, for good cause, extend the time for making returns for not longer than 30 days. No extension shall be valid unless granted in writing upon written application of the lodging provider. Such grant may not be applicable for a period longer than 12 consecutive months. A lodging provider granted an extension shall remit tax equaling not less than 100 percent of the tax paid for the corresponding period of the prior fiscal year; such remittance to be made on or before the date the tax would otherwise come due without the grant of extension. No penalty or interest shall be charged during the first ten days of the extension period. Thereafter, interest shall be collected on the unpaid balance at the rate of one percent per month.
(h) Collection fee allowed lodging providers. Lodging providers collecting the tax shall be allowed a percentage of the tax due and accounted for and shall be reimbursed in the form of a deduction in submitting, reporting and paying the amount due, if the amount is not delinquent at the time of payment. The rate of the deduction shall be three percent of the amount due, but only if the amount due was not delinquent at the time of payment.
(Ord. No. O-12-03-06, § 2(exh. A), 3-22-2012)

Administrative fee means a component of an occupation tax which approximates the reasonable cost of handling and processing the occupation tax.
Dominant line means the type of business, within a multiple-line business, that the greatest amount of income is derived from.
Gross receipts.
(1) The term "gross receipts" means the total revenue of the business or practitioner for the period, including without limitation the following:
a. Total income without deduction for the cost of goods or expenses incurred;
b. Gain from trading in stocks, bonds, capital assets, or instruments of indebtedness;
c. Proceeds from commissions on the sale of property, goods, or services;
d. Proceeds from fees for services rendered; and
e. Proceeds from rent, interest, royalty, or dividend income.
(2) The term "gross receipts" shall not include the following:
a. Sales, use, or excise tax;
b. Sales returns, allowances, and discounts;
c. Interorganizational sales or transfers between or among the units of a parent-subsidiary controlled group of corporations as defined by 26 USC 1563(a)(1), or between or among the units of a brother-sister controlled group of corporations as defined by 26 USC 1563(a)(2), or between or among a parent corporation, wholly owned subsidiaries of such parent corporation, and any corporation in which such parent corporation or one or more of its wholly owned subsidiaries owns stock possessing at least 30 percent of the total value of shares of all classes of stock of such partially owned corporation, or between or among wholly owned partnerships or other wholly owned entities;
d. Payments made to a subcontractor or an independent agent that contributed to the gross receipts in issue;
e. Governmental and foundation grants, charitable contributions, or the interest income derived from such funds received by a nonprofit organization which employs salaried practitioners otherwise covered by this chapter, if such funds constitute 80 percent or more of the organization's receipts; and

Location of office shall include any structure or vehicle where business, profession, or occupation is conducted, but shall not include a temporary or construction work site which serves a single customer or project or a vehicle used for sales or delivery by a business or practitioner of a profession or occupation which has a location or office. Governing body. The mayor and city council of the City of Americus.

City means the City of Americus.

(Ord. No. O-2012-19, 7-19-2012)

(Ord. No. O-2012-19, 7-19-2012)
748:
It is unlawful for any person to solicit or attempt to solicit at a place of residence at any entrance or part of the building other than the main entrance to the residence. (Ord. No. O-2012-19, 7-19-2012)
749:
At each dwelling, whether it is an apartment unit or private residence, the solicitor shall, at the time of initial contact with a prospective customer, identify himself or herself, identify his or her organization or corporation, and inform the occupant in unambiguous terms of the purpose of the solicitation.
(Ord. No. O-2012-19, 7-19-2012)
750:
It is unlawful for any person engaged in solicitation to misrepresent the purpose of the solicitation or use any false or deceptive statements or any misrepresentation to induce a sale or contribution, or use any plan, scheme, or ruse which misrepresents the status or purpose of the person making the call.
(Ord. No. O-2012-19, 7-19-2012)

(2) The name of the person who will be in the city and such person's address.

(4) Where business will be conducted and during what hours.

In such books there shall be entered also the full name and address of the person by whom same was deposited or sold, and the time this was done. 767:
All traveling and itinerant dealers, salespersons, and buyers of gold, silver, jewelry, coins and other precious metals shall hold such goods so pledged, traded, or purchased by them for at least seven days before disposing of them in any way.
(Code 1962, § 13-79; Code 1986, § 14-67)
768:
In the event it is determined that any item bought, sold, or traded to, or received by the traveling or itinerant dealer, salesperson or buyer is the subject of any theft or crime, the dealer, salesperson, or itinerant buyer shall, upon demand of the chief of police, or the chief's designee, surrender the same to the police department.

Vehicle for hire means and shall refer to any vehicle utilized by a person has been issued a permit to transport persons for a fee by the chief of police consistent with the provisions of this article. 773:
In order to operate a vehicle for hire business within the corporate limits of the city, the owner of such business must obtain a business license from the finance director of the city for such business. The cost of such business license, which shall be paid at the time of application and which shall be nonrefundable, shall be in an amount to be determined from time to time by the city council. The issuance of such business license for a vehicle for hire business shall not authorize the owner of the business, or any other person employed by such owner, to engage in the vehicle for hire business until such owner complies with all of the other provisions of this article.

The owner of such business shall keep on file with the chief of police documentation providing the name of the owner of the business, the owner's business address, all business telephone numbers listed in the owner's name, the names of all drivers of vehicles for hire employed by such owner, the permit number for each such driver, the home address of each such driver, and the total number of vehicles for hire that such owner operates as part of such business. (Code 1986, § 22-3; Ord. No. O-03-12-41, 12-18-2003)

Upon the issuance of a business license by the finance director to the owner of the vehicle for hire business, the finance director shall also provide to such owner a distinct serial number that shall be painted or stenciled on each vehicle for hire. One distinct serial number shall be issued to each vehicle for hire, and no two vehicles shall be authorized to use the same serial number. Such number shall be at least six inches in height and shall be placed on a conspicuous part of the vehicle for hire so that it may be visible. In addition, the name and address of the vehicle for hire business shall be displayed in a conspicuous place on all of the vehicles for hire at all times. The name of the driver shall be prominently displayed within all vehicles for hire. No vehicle for hire shall be authorized to operate within the corporate limits of the city as a vehicle for hire until compliance with the provisions of this section is completed.
(Code 1986, § 22-5; Ord. No. O-03-12-41, 12-18-2003; Ord. No. O-04-12-33, 12-16-2004)
777:
No vehicle for hire business shall operate in the city unless the owner thereof shall maintain a place of business within the corporate limits of the city.
(Code 1986, § 22-6; Ord. No. O-03-12-41, 12-18-2003)

(a) Any person, including any person who owns and operates a vehicle for hire business, who intends to drive a vehicle for hire within the corporate limits of the city, shall apply for a permit to do so from the police department. Such permit shall be applied for in writing upon such application forms as are deemed appropriate by the chief of police. Such application shall require such information as may be deemed necessary by the chief of police. Such permit shall be in addition to the vehicle for hire business license that the owner of such vehicle for hire business is required to obtain from the finance director as required by this chapter.
(b) Such permit application shall be signed by at least two individuals who are personally familiar with the applicant and can testify to the applicant's good character. No person may sign such application as a reference who either owns a vehicle for hire business or who has, or is in the process of applying for, a permit to operate a vehicle for hire as a driver. Such application shall also be signed by the applicant.

In order for a person to receive a permit to operate a vehicle for hire within the city, such person must have attained the age of at least 18 years and must possess a valid state driver's license issued by the state department of motor vehicles of the appropriate class under O.C.G.A. title 40 (O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1 et seq.) that would authorize the applicant to drive persons in a vehicle for hire. Any loss of the privilege to drive a motor vehicle arising out of or in connection with the permit holder's arrest for or violation of any of the traffic or drug statutes or ordinances of this state, any other state, or any county or municipality located in this or any other state, shall immediately invalidate any permit to operate a vehicle for hire issued under this article.
(Code 1986, § 22-8; Ord. No. O-03-12-41, 12-18-2003)
780:
Each person applying for a permit to drive a vehicle for hire shall furnish a health certificate and a vision certificate to the chief of police with such permit application. The health certificate shall be signed by a practicing physician in good standing and the vision certificate shall be signed by a practicing ophthalmologist or optometrist in good standing. The form of the certificate must be approved by the chief of police.
(Code 1986, § 22-9; Ord. No. O-03-12-41, 12-18-2003)
781:
No person shall be authorized to drive a vehicle for hire carrying passengers until such person has exhibited, upon examination by the chief of police or his designee, a familiarity with the provisions of this article and the traffic statutes, laws, ordinances, and regulations in force in the city. The chief of police shall provide at least one copy of the vehicle for hire article to each vehicle for hire driver.
(Code 1986, § 22-10; Ord. No. O-03-12-41, 12-18-2003)
782:
Each permit issued to a driver of a vehicle for hire shall expire on December 31 of the year in which such permit was issued. Applications for renewal of such permit shall be accepted by the police department between December 1 and December 31 of each calendar year, but no person shall be authorized to operate a vehicle for hire beyond December 31 of any calendar year until such person's application for a new or renewal permit is approved in accord with this article.
(Code 1986, § 22-11; Ord. No. O-03-12-41, 12-18-2003)
783:
(a) The application fee required to be paid at the time of the submission of the application for a permit as a driver of a vehicle for hire, shall not be prorated.
(b) The permit issued to a successful applicant shall be numbered, dated as of the date of issue, and shall have such other information displayed thereon as may be deemed appropriate by the chief of police.
(c) The permit shall, at all times when the permittee is engaged in driving a vehicle for hire within the city, be displayed in a conspicuous place by said permittee in the vehicle so that the permit can be easily seen by passengers riding in said vehicle for hire.
(Code 1986, § 22-12; Ord. No. O-03-12-41, 12-18-2003)
784:
(a) Each applicant for a vehicle for hire business license shall, before the license is granted, provide evidence of a policy or certificate of motor vehicle liability insurance, with respect to each vehicle to be operated as a vehicle for hire, with coverage in the following amounts:

(2) Twenty-five thousand dollars for injury to more than one person in any one accident; and

(Code 1986, § 22-13; Ord. No. O-03-12-41, 12-18-2003)
785:
The rates charged by vehicles for hire must be posted in the vehicle, for inspection by passengers at all times.
(Code 1986, § 22-14; Ord. No. O-03-12-41, 12-18-2003)
786:
Each person who drives a vehicle for hire upon the streets of the city shall submit to inspection of both the vehicle and the driver by a certified police officer of the city police department whenever directed to do so.
(Code 1986, § 22-15; Ord. No. O-03-12-41, 12-18-2003)
787:
(a) In the event that the owner of the vehicle for hire business fails to comply with any of the provisions of this article, the finance director shall be authorized to suspend or revoke the business license previously issued to such owner. In the event of such a suspension or revocation, notice of such decision shall be communicated to the owner in writing by personal service or by certified mail, return receipt requested. Any suspension hereunder shall be for such duration as the finance director deems appropriate, but any such suspension shall not exceed 30 calendar days. Such appeal must be in writing, must be submitted to the city official who ordered such suspension or revocation, and must set out the grounds upon which the appellant contends that the suspension or revocation was erroneously issued. The city manager of the city shall be notified of the filing of such an appeal and shall schedule a hearing thereon by the city council within 30 calendar days from the date of filing such appeal. In considering such appeal, the city council shall affirm the action or decision of the finance director or the chief of police, as the case may be, if the city council finds that such decision was supported by any evidence.

798:
(a) Mobile food truck shall mean a retail food establishment that is not a permanent restaurant that serves food or drink to the public. Mobile food trucks shall be classified as one of the following types of mobile food trucks:
(1) A retail mobile food truck is a retail mobile food establishment from which the owner or operator thereof cooks, prepares, sells, serves, or delivers food, food-related items, to individual purchasers within the corporate limits of the city.
(2) A temporary mobile food truck is a mobile food truck from which the owner or operator thereof cooks, prepares, sells, serves, or delivers food, food-related items, to individual purchasers where the owner or operator only intends to operate at fixed locations in conjunction with single events lasting no more than two consecutive days at a time hosted or sponsored by either the city, a department of the city, an authority established by the city, or a USCS 26 § 501(C)(3) non-profit legal entity. The owner or operator of such temporary mobile food truck must register with the city clerk as a temporary mobile food truck prior to operating its business in the city, and shall be required to keep a copy of such registration in the temporary mobile food truck at all times while conducting its business in the city. A mobile food truck shall not be classified as a temporary mobile food truck if the owner or operator of the mobile food truck participates in more than two such hosted or sponsored events during a calendar year. In the event that the temporary mobile food truck seeks to operate its mobile food truck in more than two such events within a calendar year, then a mobile food truck license must be applied for and obtained in accord with this article.
(b) Food service permit shall mean a food service establishment permit which is required from the Georgia Department of Public Health which allows a mobile food truck to operate within the corporate limits of the city.
(Ord. No. O-2023-05, 5-18-2023)
799:
Mobile food trucks shall be authorized to cook, prepare, sell, serve, and deliver food, food-related items, and beverages within the corporate limits of the city from a mobile food truck. Any mobile food truck, whether owned or operated by an individual, corporate, or other legal entity, shall only be authorized to operate as a mobile food truck in accord with this article if the person or legal entity owning or operating the mobile food truck obtains an appropriate food service permit from the Georgia Department of Public Health and pays for and obtains the applicable business licenses, occupation fees, and regulatory fees imposed pursuant to article IV of chapter 46 of the city's Code of Ordinances. Notwithstanding the foregoing, a temporary mobile food truck shall not be required to pay city business licenses, occupation fees, and regulatory fees as long as it remains classified as a temporary mobile food truck, but shall be required to obtain a food service permit as required by O.C.G.A. § 26-2-371 prior to being operated in the corporate limits of the city.
(Ord. No. O-2023-05, 5-18-2023)
801:
(a) The owner and operator of a mobile food truck shall comply with all federal, state, and local health and safety regulations and requirements, and shall maintain any and all licenses required by any other health organization or governmental organization having jurisdiction over the mobile food truck.
(b) The license or registration issued by the city under which the mobile food truck is operating is to be firmly attached and visible on the retail mobile food truck at all times while customers are being served.
(c) Food sales shall only be conducted from the mobile food truck and customer seating shall not be provided by the mobile food truck vendor.
(d) Except as may be authorized as part of a city-approved special event, mobile food trucks shall not be left unattended or stored at any time on the vending site when sales to customers are not taking place or during restricted hours of operation.
(e) The following safety regulations shall apply to any and all mobile food trucks:
(1) Every mobile food truck shall be equipped with reverse signal alarm with a sound distinguishable from the surrounding noise level.
(2) Every mobile food truck shall be equipped with two rear vision mirrors, one on each side, firmly attached to the outside of the mobile food truck, and so located as to reflect to the drive a view of the highway to the rear, along both sides of the vehicle.
(3) Any driver of a mobile food truck must possess a valid Georgia's driver's license and each mobile food truck must operate from a motorized wheeled vehicle that may be lawfully driven upon the streets and roadways within the city.
(Ord. No. O-2023-05, 5-18-2023)
802:
(a) No mobile food truck shall operate its business on any public or private property without the written consent of the owner of such property, a copy of which shall be maintained in the mobile food truck.
(b) No mobile food trucks shall operate its business within 15 feet of any street, intersection, or pedestrian walkway or within ten feet of any public or private driveway.
(c) No mobile food truck shall conduct its business in the public right-of-way.
(d) Except as may be allowed as part of a city-approved special event, a mobile food truck shall only be permitted to operate its business on a given property for no more than two consecutive days and no more than ten days in any calendar month. A minimum of two calendar days must transpire between operating periods on any given property.
(e) Except as may be allowed as part of a city-approved special event, while operating its business, a mobile food truck may occupy no more than ten percent of designated parking spaces on a given property, and at no time shall the operation of a mobile food truck on private property reduce the number of parking spaces on a property below the minimum number of parking spaces required by the city Code.
(f) The placement or location of a mobile food truck while operating its business shall not impede the flow of traffic, be placed on the right-of-way, or cause any potential safety hazards to pedestrians or vehicles.
(g) Except as may be allowed as part of a city-approved special event, a mobile food truck shall not operate its business within 200 feet of the nearest corner of any existing food establishment during such establishment's hours of operation without prior written permission from the food service establishment, a copy of which shall be maintained in the mobile food truck.
(h) Mobile food trucks shall not operate its business within 200 feet of any city-sponsored special event unless the mobile food truck is licensed, is operating as part of the city-sponsored event, or is operating as a temporary mobile food truck as part of such special event.
(i) No mobile food truck shall operate its business while parked in a designated public parking place on the streets of the city.
(j) No mobile food truck shall sell or offer to sell, offer to sell, serve, or deliver any alcoholic beverages to its customers or to any other persons at any time.
(k) No mobile food truck shall allow customers to consume food, food related items, or beverages inside of the mobile food truck.
(l) No mobile food truck shall operate its business upon the property of any public school system, private school system, property of a college or the technical college system of Georgia, property of a university of the university system of Georgia, without written permission from the school, technical college, or local unit of the university system to do so.
(m) No mobile food truck shall stop, stand, or park in lanes of motor vehicle traffic on public rights-of-way within the city except where otherwise required to do so by applicable traffic laws and regulations.
(n) No mobile food truck shall utilize microphones, megaphones, loudspeakers, loud bells, whistles, or similar attention-getting sound equipment to advertise its food products.
(o) A mobile food truck shall operate its business only in the commercial areas of the city, and shall not operate its business in the residential areas of the city.
(Ord. No. O-2023-05, 5-18-2023)
803:
In accord with the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 26-2-379, the city may not refuse to license a mobile food truck or a temporary mobile food truck solely because the mobile food truck has a food service permit issued in a county other than Sumter County in the State of Georgia. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Sumter County Board of Health shall be authorized to verify that a food service permit is in good standing and that there are no public health or safety concerns with respect to a mobile food truck or a temporary mobile food truck seeking to operate within the corporate limits of the city. In addition, both a mobile food truck and a temporary mobile food truck shall be subject to periodic and unannounced inspections by the Sumter County Board of Health notwithstanding the existence of an existing license from the city to operate within the corporate limits of the city.
(Ord. No. O-2023-05, 5-18-2023)

The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to the parking of recreational vehicles on property owned and controlled by a nursing home or convalescent home where the following conditions are met:
(1) The area where such recreational vehicles are to be parked is paved with asphalt or other suitable paving material and is not larger than 15,000 square feet.
(2) The area where the recreational vehicles are to be parked is not located adjacent to a city street or state highway but is located at least 500 feet from the right-of-way of any city street or state highway.
(3) No occupant of any recreational vehicle may reside at such location for more than 30 consecutive days and that there are no more than ten recreational vehicles parked at such location at any one time.
(4) The owner of the nursing home or convalescent home shall be authorized to establish electrical connections and running water connections to the area set aside for the parking of such recreational vehicles, but such electrical connections and water connections shall, in all respects comply with the other provisions of this Code.
(5) Under no circumstances shall any sewage from such recreational vehicles be disposed of in the city's sewerage system, but the owner of the nursing home or convalescent home shall be responsible for ensuring that all such sewage is disposed of properly in appropriate locations.
(6) The owner or operator of any recreational vehicle parked in accord with the terms of this section shall not be required to pay any rent or lease for the space utilized by such vehicle; nor shall such owner or operator be charged for the use of any electricity or water at such location.
(7) Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing herein shall prohibit the owner of a recreational vehicle who resides at a nursing home or convalescent center from parking his recreational vehicle at such location during such times and for such lengths of time as he or she may deem appropriate, and the nursing home or convalescent center shall be authorized to permit the owners of such recreational vehicles to connect to the electrical and water connections at such parking area.
